en.title: Fewest Clicks in a Web Link Simulator
en.description:
Each directed link lets one click jump from u to v; get_links(page) returns the targets of all outgoing edges of that page. Find the minimum number of clicks from start to target; it is 0 if they are the same, and −1 if target is unreachable. Duplicate links and self-loops are allowed.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains m, followed by m lines of u v, and the last line contains start target. 1≤m≤200000, and page names are strings without whitespace. This site's transport protocol adds that a single name has at most 16 Unicode characters (the original 200,000 edges are kept, and the worst-case UTF-8 input is at most 26,000,500 bytes). Names are case-sensitive and need not be pure English.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 2; -1; 0. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Build an outgoing adjacency list to simulate get_links, then run BFS from start and return the level at which target is first discovered.
